title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer regional failover quorum calculation to prevent thrashing
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Fixes incorrect quorum calculation in SLO enforcer that could cause regional failover thrashing; deploy as hotfix.
description:
Motivation: In production we observed repeated regional failover thrashing during partial outages (see incident SUP-9012). The SLO enforcer was mis-evaluating region quorum availability in edge cases where draining / cordoned replicas were still included in a naive capacity fraction. This caused rapid failover decisions and subsequent rollback/failback cycles under bursty load.

What this change does: Adjusts the regional quorum calculation to use weighted healthy_capacity (excludes draining/drained instances and respects per-replica weight) instead of simple available/total fraction. Adds hysteresis (30s sample smoothing) and a cooldown window (5m after failover) to avoid oscillation. Adds unit and integration tests that simulate partial-region failures and validates stability.

Files touched: slo-enforcer quorum logic, tests, deployment overlay for hotfix rollout, docs playbook update, and alert tuning for the enforcer.

Checklist:
- [x] Repro case added to integration tests (regional_failover_test.go)
- [x] Unit tests for quorum weighting (quorum_test.go)
- [x] Added cooldown/hysteresis with configurable defaults
- [x] Updated incident playbook and alert thresholds
- [x] CI green and manual canary deployed to us-west-2

Testing and validation: Ran unit test suite, integration failure-simulation harness against staging, and a controlled canary in us-west-2 for 30 minutes under synthetic partial-region load. Observed no failover thrashing and SLO enforcer behaved within expected thresholds.

Rollback plan: Revert this PR and redeploy previous slo-enforcer image (tag prior to this change). Alerting will detect deviation in failover rate within 5 minutes.

Related: ENG-4872 (root cause investigation), SRE-120 (post-incident action items).
